set.title: [bsk] Beskar v1 spec: glossary, ADRs and build spec
set.body:
## Destination

A v1 spec set for the restarted Beskar: a root `CONTEXT.md` glossary, ADRs in `docs/adr/` for hard-to-reverse choices, and a build spec that builder agents can implement as a Rust workspace of crates. The map produces decisions, not product code.

## Notes

- **Source brief:** `docs/BRIEF.md`. Beskar keeps one Library of agent skills, groups them into Profiles, and copies the union of a workspace's enabled Profiles into `<workspace>/.agents/skills/`. It detects drift so it never destroys local edits.
- **v1 scope:** `init` and `doctor`; the `library`, `profile`, `repo` and `registry` command groups; reconciliation with `--dry-run`; fingerprints and drift detection; the conflict prompt; a non-interactive conflict policy; promote; adoption of existing `.agents/skills` content, including skm stamps.
- **Platforms:** Linux, macOS and Windows.
- **Stack:** Rust, as a workspace of crates.
- **Prior art:** the old v0.1.0 (Git-backed Library, TUI, GUI) at commit `6162707`. Read it with `git show 6162707:docs/SPEC.md` (and `git show 6162707:<path>` for code) to find edge cases. The brief wins every conflict, and nothing carries over by default.
- **Where decisions go:** glossary terms go in a root `CONTEXT.md` (glossary only, no implementation detail). Hard-to-reverse choices go in `docs/adr/`. The crate-boundaries ticket splits these per crate later and updates `docs/agents/domain.md` to match.
- **Every session:** work on its own branch from `main`. Commit `CONTEXT.md`, ADR and `.rohrpost/` changes as they happen. Merge to `main` when done.
- **Skills:** grilling and domain-modeling on every ticket; codebase-design on the crate-boundaries ticket; prototype on the conflict-handling ticket; research through a subagent for research tickets; unslop on all written docs.

## Decisions so far

<!-- the index: one line per closed ticket, enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link for the detail the ticket holds -->

## Not yet specified

- The form of the build spec handed to builder agents, and the build phase order.
- The test strategy: hermetic filesystem tests, fixtures, cross-platform CI.
- The error model and the style of user-facing messages.
- Platform-specific rules (Windows paths, case-insensitive names, the executable bit). These become specifiable once skill identity and the drift model are decided.

## Out of scope

- The AI classifier (categories, tags, suggested profiles). The brief (§12) makes it optional enrichment for later.
- TUI and GUI. CLI first, UI later.
- Git features (sync, remotes, branches). Git is an external concern for the Library.
- Rich skill metadata (tags, category, version, dependencies). v1 reads only `name` and `description`.
- A symlink install mode. v1 installs copies.

set.title: [bsk-1] What do the Agent Skills spec and harnesses require of a skill directory?
set.body:
## Question

What does the Agent Skills format (agentskills.io) require of a skill directory, and which agent harnesses read project skills from `<workspace>/.agents/skills/`?

Find out:

- The required and optional `SKILL.md` frontmatter fields.
- The name rules: allowed characters, length, and whether the folder name must equal `name`.
- The expected subdirectories (`scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`, others), any limits on files, and whether a skill may contain nested skills.
- For each major harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, others with public docs): which paths it reads for project-level skills, whether it follows symlinks (this repo links `.claude/skills` to `.agents/skills`), and how deep it looks.

Use primary sources only. The findings feed the tickets on skill identity and on the install target.

set.title: [bsk-2] Which maintained Rust crates cover YAML, prompts, diff, locks and atomic writes?
set.body:
## Question

Which maintained Rust crates should the v1 build use for each of these jobs?

- YAML read **and** write for profiles. `serde_yaml` is deprecated; the old build used `serde-saphyr` with deserialization only, and profiles must now also be written.
- Interactive prompts that fall back cleanly when stdin is not a TTY.
- Text diff for the conflict prompt's "show diff".
- Advisory file locks on Linux, macOS and Windows (std `File::try_lock` compared with `fs4`).
- Atomic file replace and directory swap. Can a non-empty directory be replaced atomically on each platform?
- Directory walking, SHA-256, and the CLI parser.

For each crate give its maintenance status, licence, MSRV and platform caveats. The findings feed the tickets on the profile model, the drift model, conflict handling and reconciliation safety.

set.title: [bsk-3] Skill identity and content boundary
set.body:
## Question

What identifies a skill, and which files are part of it?

- **Identity:** the folder name, the `SKILL.md` `name`, or a fixed id? Must the folder name and `name` match? Which name rules apply (see the Agent Skills research ticket)? What happens on a rename in the Library, both to Profiles that reference the skill and to workspaces that have it installed?
- **Library layout:** a flat `skills/<name>/`, or nested groups (the old spec's "buckets", §9 and §13)?
- **Validity:** what makes a directory a valid skill? Is `SKILL.md` required, and are `name` and `description` required? What does Beskar do with an invalid skill?
- **Content boundary:** which files count as skill content for copying and fingerprinting? Decide for symlinks, special files, dotfiles, nested `.git` directories, OS clutter such as `.DS_Store`, Beskar's own stamp, and `.skm.json`.

Facts: `.agents/skills/codemap` in this repo is a Git checkout with its own `.git`. Prior art: old spec §5, §8.2, §11, §12 and §118. There, name = folder = `SKILL.md` name, names are globally unique, there is no fixed id, and symlinks and special files are rejected.

set.title: [bsk-4] Profile model
set.body:
## Question

What is a Profile, exactly?

- The YAML schema of `profiles/<name>.yaml` (brief §5), including a schema version.
- **Identity:** the file name, the `name` field, or a fixed id? What happens to Registry entries when a Profile is renamed or deleted, including when this happens on another machine that syncs the Library?
- A Profile that references a skill that is not in the Library: is that invalid, a warning, or skipped?
- Can a Profile include other Profiles? Does skill order mean anything? Are empty Profiles allowed?

Prior art: old spec §15–17 and §28. There, Profiles are TOML with a fixed UUID and an ordered list, with no nesting, and the Registry points at the UUID so renames are safe.

set.title: [bsk-5] Workspace identity and install target
set.body:
## Question

What identifies a workspace, and where do its skills go?

- **Term:** does the glossary say "repository" or "workspace"? The brief uses both (§2).
- **Identity:** the canonical absolute path? Decide the cases of symlinked paths, case-insensitive filesystems, and a workspace inside another workspace.
- **Moved or deleted workspaces:** what do status and `registry prune` report, and how does the user point a registration at the new location?
- **Current workspace:** how do commands such as `repo enable` find the workspace from the working directory? Walk up to a registered path, or require an explicit path?
- **Target:** always `<workspace>/.agents/skills`, or a per-workspace override of `agent_skills_path`? One target or several, for example `.claude/skills` for harnesses that do not read `.agents/skills` (see the Agent Skills research ticket)?

Prior art: old spec §5 "Workspace", §24 and §26. There, adapters are `agents`, `claude` and custom, and there is one installation per (workspace, target) pair.

set.title: [bsk-6] Beskar home, config and registry storage
set.body:
## Question

Where does Beskar keep its state, and in which formats?

- **Default home:** `~/.beskar` (the brief) or platform directories such as XDG and AppData (old spec §85)? Does the default Library sit inside the home?
- **Config:** the file format and keys (`library_path`, `registry_path`, `agent_skills_path`, settings), plus environment overrides (old spec §86: `BESKAR_HOME`, `BESKAR_LIBRARY`).
- **Registry:** the file format and schema version; one file or one per workspace; what happens with a schema version Beskar does not know (old spec §129 fails closed).
- **Initialization:** what `init` and `library init` create, and what they do when state already exists, for example an existing Library to adopt.

Where installed fingerprints live (Registry or a stamp in each skill) belongs to the drift-model ticket, not this one.

set.title: [bsk-7] Drift model and fingerprints
set.body:
## Question

How does Beskar know whether an installed skill is clean, outdated, or modified locally?

- **Granularity:** one hash per skill or a per-file manifest? Only a manifest can tell extra files apart from edits and find files that the Library deleted (old spec §31 and §8.6).
- **What gets hashed:** bytes only, or also the executable bit and empty directories? Line endings?
- **Storage:** does the installed fingerprint live in the Registry, in a stamp file inside each installed skill, or in both? What happens when a stamp is deleted or edited by hand?
- **The full state list,** beyond the brief's three states (§10). For example: library changed and locally modified at the same time; missing from the workspace; extra files; a same-name folder that Beskar did not install; a skill that no Profile wants any more; a skill removed from the Library. The old spec lists 18 states in §38.
- How status output shows each state.

set.title: [bsk-8] Conflict handling: dry-run output, prompt and non-interactive policy
set.body:
## Question

How should the dry-run output and the conflict prompt look and behave? Answer this with a rough prototype over the states from the drift-model ticket.

- The `repo update --dry-run` plan output (brief §7).
- The interactive prompt (brief §11): keep local, replace with library, promote to library, show diff. Does "keep local" last beyond one run as a pin, or does the conflict come back next time?
- **Non-interactive policy:** which flags exist, and what is the default when no flag is given (fail or skip)?
- **`--all` across workspaces:** when one workspace has a conflict, does Beskar abort everything, skip that workspace, or ask per conflict?
- A same-name folder that Beskar did not install: the same prompt, or separate consent (old spec §49, `--replace-unmanaged`)?

Prior art: old spec §47–49.

set.title: [bsk-9] Promote semantics
set.body:
## Question

What does promote do?

- **The basic case:** copy a locally modified installed skill back into the Library, then mark the workspace copy clean.
- **The Library copy also changed since install:** refuse, show a three-way diff, or overwrite?
- **A skill created in a workspace that is not in the Library:** can promote add it, and to which Profile?
- **Other workspaces:** do they update right after promote, or at the next update?
- **Command name and place:** `skill promote`, `repo promote`, or `library promote`? The brief (§10) leaves the name open.

Prior art: the old spec does not cover this. The nearest feature is `ingest --replace` (§70).

set.title: [bsk-10] Reconciliation safety
set.body:
## Question

How does reconciliation apply a plan without losing data?

- Plan everything, then apply (old spec §45)? Does `--dry-run` use the same planner?
- **Replacement unit:** a per-skill atomic replace (stage, then rename) or file by file (old spec §59)? In what order are files, the stamp and the Registry written (old spec §8.7 and §61)?
- **Locks** on the Registry, the Library and each target (old spec §88). What happens when a lock is held?
- **Crash recovery:** re-running only, or a journal (old spec §128)?
- **No Git snapshot:** the Library can change between plan and apply. Are hashes checked again before each write?
- **Missing Profiles:** a Profile that is missing or unreadable must never turn into "remove all its skills" (old spec §39–40 and §58). How is last-applied membership kept?

set.title: [bsk-11] Library ingest: add, scan and remove
set.body:
## Question

How do `library add`, `library scan` and `library remove` behave?

- Validation on import (using the rules from the skill-identity ticket), and partial imports.
- **Name collisions:** a name that already exists in the Library is refused, replaced, or renamed? What about duplicates inside the scanned source?
- Stripping stamps (`.skm.json`, Beskar's own) and other non-content files on import.
- Copy or move from the source.
- **`scan`:** its depth, what it treats as a skill root, and the confirm prompt with its non-interactive form.
- **`library remove`:** what happens to a skill that Profiles still reference or workspaces still have installed?

Prior art: old spec §70–71.

set.title: [bsk-12] Adoption of existing .agents/skills content, including skm stamps
set.body:
## Question

What does Beskar do when a workspace's `.agents/skills` already holds skills at registration or at the first update?

- **Same content as a Library skill:** adopt it as a clean install?
- **Same name, different content:** treat it as local drift or as unmanaged, or ask the user?
- **No Library match:** leave it alone as unmanaged, offer to ingest it, or offer to promote it?
- **skm stamps:** convert `.skm.json` into Beskar's installed fingerprint, or ignore the stamps and compare content?

Facts: real skm stamps in this repo have the shape `{"skm":1,"source":"<name>","collectionCommit":"<sha>","files":{"<path>":"sha256:<hex>"}}`, with no executable flag. The old `migrate.rs` assumed a different shape. This repo's own `.agents/skills` is managed by skm, and `codemap` in it is a Git checkout. Prior art: old spec §120–124.

set.title: [bsk-13] CLI surface and automation contract
set.body:
## Question

What is the final v1 command tree, and what is its contract for scripts?

- Start from the brief's tree (§15). Resolve the overlap between `repo update --all`, `registry update --all` and a top-level `update --all`. Which aliases (`status`, `update`) ship in v1?
- `repo enable` on an unregistered workspace: an error, or an implicit `repo add`? Confirm that `enable` changes desired state only (brief §6).
- `profile add` for a skill that is not in the Library; `profile delete` of a Profile that workspaces use.
- **Registry inspection:** `list`, `status`, `stats`, "where is skill X used", and `prune`.
- The checks that `doctor` runs.
- **Automation:** `--json` output, exit codes (old spec §92–94 and §130), and which commands take `--dry-run`.

set.title: [bsk-14] Crate boundaries and bounded contexts
set.body:
## Question

How is the Rust workspace split into crates, and where do the bounded contexts sit?

- The crate list and the direction of dependencies between crates.
- The seam that keeps domain logic free of CLI presentation (brief §17, "CLI first, UI later").
- Where filesystem effects sit relative to a pure planner, for testability.
- Split the root `CONTEXT.md` into a `CONTEXT.md` per crate plus a `CONTEXT-MAP.md`, as `docs/agents/domain.md` expects, or change `domain.md` to describe a single context.

Use the codebase-design skill.

text:
## Resolution

**Findings:** `docs/research/agent-skills-format.md` on branch `research/agent-skills-format` (commit `45942da`). Read it with `git show research/agent-skills-format:docs/research/agent-skills-format.md`. Every claim cites a primary source. 21 gaps are marked UNCONFIRMED.

- **Frontmatter:** `name` (1-64 chars) and `description` (1-1024 chars) are required. The only optional fields are `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (string to string) and `allowed-tools` (experimental). The reference validator and claude.ai uploads reject other top-level keys. Harnesses accept their own extra keys, and several relax the required fields.
- **Name rules:** lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens; no leading or trailing hyphen; no `--`; must equal the folder name. Enforcement varies: VS Code and Roo refuse a mismatch, while Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Goose and Pi accept one. `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, at most 64 ASCII characters and equal to the folder name, loads in every harness checked. Claude Code reserves `synced` and `anthropic-skills`.
- **Layout:** `scripts/`, `references/` and `assets/` are conventions only, and any other files are allowed. There are no hard file limits. The spec says nothing about nested skills (spec issues #137, #59 and #15 are open).
- **Who reads `<workspace>/.agents/skills/`:** Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot (CLI and VS Code), Amp, OpenCode, Goose, Roo, Factory, Pi, Junie and Devin Desktop. **Claude Code reads only `.claude/skills/`** (request #16345 is open). Kiro documents only `.kiro/skills/`.
- **Depth:** Claude Code, VS Code and Gemini read one level (`<root>/<name>/SKILL.md`). Codex recurses 6 levels. Goose and OpenCode recurse with no limit. A flat layout is the only one every harness reads the same way, and a `SKILL.md` nested inside a skill becomes an extra skill in some harnesses.
- **Symlinks:** documented for Claude Code (per-skill entries), Codex, Copilot CLI and Roo; OpenCode and Goose follow them in their source code. Cursor, VS Code, Amp and the others are UNCONFIRMED.
- **Discovery root:** Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi and Claude Code walk from the working directory up to the repo root. Gemini and Goose read only the working directory. Gemini and Junie skip project skills in untrusted folders.

The considerations for Beskar (the research file's last section) go to the tickets on skill identity, the install target and reconciliation safety. They are not decisions.

reason: Name = folder, ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ up to 64 chars; flat layout; every major harness reads .agents/skills except Claude Code (.claude/skills only) and Kiro

text: Research input from [bsk-1] (see research/agent-skills-format:docs/research/agent-skills-format.md): the spec requires the folder name to equal `name`, matching ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ with at most 64 chars. Harnesses enforce this unevenly, and Claude Code reserves `synced` and `anthropic-skills`. Harnesses disagree on depth (1 level, 6 levels, or unlimited), so a SKILL.md nested inside a skill becomes an extra skill in some of them.

Research input from [bsk-1] (see research/agent-skills-format:docs/research/agent-skills-format.md): Claude Code reads only .claude/skills/, and Kiro documents only .kiro/skills/. Every other major harness reads .agents/skills/. Claude Code documents per-skill symlinks only; this repo's whole-directory .claude/skills symlink works but is not documented. Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi and Claude Code walk up from the working directory to the repo root. Gemini and Goose read only the working directory.

Research input from [bsk-1] (see research/agent-skills-format:docs/research/agent-skills-format.md): Goose and OpenCode recurse without a depth limit and scan hidden folders. A staging or backup folder under .agents/skills/ that contains a SKILL.md would therefore show up as a duplicate skill. Keep staging outside the target, or make sure it never holds a SKILL.md.

- **[bsk-1] What do the Agent Skills spec and harnesses require of a skill directory?** (`s3shzq`): name = folder name, `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` up to 64 chars; only a flat layout reads the same in every harness; every major harness reads `.agents/skills/` except Claude Code (`.claude/skills/` only) and Kiro.

text:
## Resolution

**Findings:** `docs/research/rust-crates.md` on branch `research/rust-crates` (commit `54abdf0`). Read it with `git show research/rust-crates:docs/research/rust-crates.md`. Every claim cites its source. The key behaviours were checked in a scratch crate on Linux aarch64 with Rust 1.98.1. Claims about macOS and Windows come from docs and source code only.

| Job | Recommended | Runner-up |
|---|---|---|
| YAML read + write | `serde-saphyr` 1.3.0 (default features; serializes too) | `serde_norway` 0.9.42 (stale since 2024-12) |
| Prompts | `dialoguer` 0.12.0, called only after Beskar's own TTY check | `inquire` 0.9.4 |
| Diff | `similar` 3.2.0 | `diffy` 0.5.2 |
| Locks | std `File::lock`/`try_lock` (Rust 1.89+) | `fs4` 1.1.0 |
| Atomic single-file write | `atomic-write-file` 0.3.1 (fsyncs file and directory) | `tempfile` `persist` plus manual fsync |
| Directory replace | `rustix` `renameat_with(EXCHANGE)` on Linux and macOS APFS, plus a portable rename-aside fallback | none |
| Directory walk | `walkdir` 2.5.0, sorted by file name | `ignore` (skips hidden and gitignored files by default, so wrong for fingerprints) |
| SHA-256 | `sha2` 0.11 (no `io::Write`; use `digest-io` or a read loop) | `sha2` 0.10.9 |
| CLI | `clap` 4.6.7 | none |
| Home dir | `etcetera` 0.11.0 or `std::env::home_dir` | `dirs` 7.0.0 |

- **Avoid `serde_yml`:** RUSTSEC-2025-0068 lists it as unsound and unmaintained, and its repo is archived.
- **YAML quoting:** `serde-saphyr` quotes `yes`, `on` and `no`, so YAML 1.1 readers do not load them as booleans.
- **Prompts and TTYs:** every prompt crate either prompts on `/dev/tty` even when stdin is piped, or silently answers yes at end-of-file (`demand`). Beskar must check `IsTerminal` itself.
- **Windows locks:** they block other processes from reading the locked file, so lock a separate lock file.
- **Directory swap:** a non-empty directory can be swapped atomically only on Linux (`RENAME_EXCHANGE`) and macOS APFS (`RENAME_SWAP`). Windows cannot do it, and a directory rename there fails if any file inside is open. Plain `rename` onto a non-empty directory fails with `EEXIST` or `ENOTEMPTY`.
- **MSRV:** the recommended set needs Rust 1.89. `cargo-audit` found no advisories.
- **Unconfirmed:** Windows behaviour of the prompt crates; `cliclack` MSRV; a suspected memory-safety bug in `unsafe-libyaml-norway`.

These are recommendations only. Crate choices are fixed when the build spec is written.

reason: serde-saphyr for YAML read+write, dialoguer behind Beskar's own TTY check, similar, std File::lock, atomic-write-file, walkdir, sha2 0.11, clap; atomic dir swap only on Linux and macOS APFS

text: Research input from [bsk-2] (see research/rust-crates:docs/research/rust-crates.md): serde-saphyr 1.3.0 reads and writes YAML and quotes yes/on/no, so YAML 1.1 readers do not load them as booleans. Avoid serde_yml (RUSTSEC-2025-0068).

Research input from [bsk-2] (see research/rust-crates:docs/research/rust-crates.md): walk with walkdir sorted by file name for a deterministic order. The ignore crate skips hidden and gitignored files by default, so it would leave files out of fingerprints. sha2 0.11 no longer implements io::Write; use the digest-io wrapper or a read loop.

Research input from [bsk-2] (see research/rust-crates:docs/research/rust-crates.md): no prompt crate detects piped stdin reliably. dialoguer, inquire and cliclack still prompt on /dev/tty, and demand's confirm answers yes at end-of-file. Beskar must check std::io::IsTerminal before it prompts, so the non-interactive policy depends on that check, not on the prompt library. similar 3.2.0 renders unified diffs, has a bytes mode, and supports three-way merges.

Research input from [bsk-2] (see research/rust-crates:docs/research/rust-crates.md): a non-empty directory can be swapped atomically only on Linux (renameat2 RENAME_EXCHANGE) and macOS APFS (RENAME_SWAP). Windows cannot swap directories, and a directory rename there fails if any file inside is open. The portable fallback is stage next to the target, rename the old copy aside, move the new copy in, keep a recovery record. Plain rename onto a non-empty directory fails with EEXIST or ENOTEMPTY. std File::lock (Rust 1.89+) locks block other processes from reading on Windows, so lock a separate lock file. atomic-write-file fsyncs both the file and its directory; tempfile persist does not.

- **[bsk-1] What do the Agent Skills spec and harnesses require of a skill directory?** (`s3shzq`): name = folder name, `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` up to 64 chars; only a flat layout reads the same in every harness; every major harness reads `.agents/skills/` except Claude Code (`.claude/skills/` only) and Kiro.
- **[bsk-2] Which maintained Rust crates cover YAML, prompts, diff, locks and atomic writes?** (`m7n9ck`): `serde-saphyr` (read + write), `dialoguer` behind Beskar's own TTY check, `similar`, std `File::lock`, `atomic-write-file`, sorted `walkdir`, `sha2`, `clap`; atomic directory swap works only on Linux and macOS APFS.

## Not yet specified

- The form of the build spec handed to builder agents, and the build phase order.
- The test strategy: hermetic filesystem tests, fixtures, cross-platform CI.
- The error model and the style of user-facing messages.
- Platform-specific rules (Windows paths, case-insensitive names, the executable bit). These become specifiable once skill identity and the drift model are decided.

## Out of scope

- The AI classifier (categories, tags, suggested profiles). The brief (§12) makes it optional enrichment for later.
- TUI and GUI. CLI first, UI later.
- Git features (sync, remotes, branches). Git is an external concern for the Library.
- Rich skill metadata (tags, category, version, dependencies). v1 reads only `name` and `description`.
- A symlink install mode. v1 installs copies.
